title: The Amazon tax
author: herbertl
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: It’s not technically a tax. Taxes produce valuable public benefits, like medical research and parks. This is simply legal theft.

Amazon makes nearly a billion dollars in profit from search ads. Every week. Each week, they sell merchants and publishers enough search-distorting ads to capture a billion dollars in revenue. Amazon makes enough in search ad revenue to give every single one of their employees a $35,000 cash bonus and still have change left over.
My publisher is terrific, and they’re working hard to introduce people to my new book. Last week, they began buying search ads on Amazon.
At first glance, this is compelling. Someone who isn’t sure what they’re looking for, who is looking for a book or a kitchen appliance, might find one if the right ad showed up at the right time.
But of course, that’s not what yields, or what most of the ads you see on Amazon do.

Amazon makes nearly a billion dollars in profit from search ads. Every week. Each week, they sell merchants and publishers enough search-distorting ads to capture a billion dollars in revenue. Amazon makes enough in search ad revenue to give every single one of their employees a $35,000 cash bonus and still have change left over.

comments.author: ulrikrasmussen
comments.textRawHtml: I see the exact same thing on Play Store, and I think Google is outright complicit in fraud. The top result when you search for an app, even if by exact name, is always, literally 100% of the time, not the app you are looking for, but some other ad-infested knockoff spyware shit whose developer paid Google to be placed before the real thing.
comments.textZhHtml: 我在 Play 商店中看到了完全相同的内容，我认为 Google 完全是欺诈行为的同谋。当你搜索某个应用时，即使是按确切名称搜索，最上面的结果也总是 100%，不是你正在寻找的应用，而是其他一些广告泛滥的山寨间谍软件，其开发者付钱给 Google，让其排在真正的应用之前。

children.author: Frieren
children.textRawHtml:
No regulations -> fraud and scams

Expecting that the rich will do the right thing out of their good hearts is not just naive but actively damaging for society.
children.textZhHtml:
没有法规 -> 欺诈和骗局

期望富人会出于好心做正确的事不仅是天真，而且对社会造成积极破坏。

children.author: gyulai
children.textRawHtml: You forget a third option.  A monopolist doing the right thing from their good heart?  Not gonna work.  Legislators micromanaging every last aspect of every last thing through regulations?  Not gonna work.  Legislators squashing monopolies and making rules to keep competition intact and put meaningful choice into consumers' hands: Might work.
children.textZhHtml: 您忘记了第三个选项。  垄断者是出于善意做正确的事吗？  不会工作。  立法者通过法规对每件事的每一个方面进行微观管理？  不会工作。  立法者打破垄断并制定规则以保持竞争完整并将有意义的选择交到消费者手中：可能会奏效。

children.author: bubblegumcrisis
children.textRawHtml:
Huh.. That is an interesting idea. I like it.

You have a company, it is worth below X dollars? You do what you want. Above X dollars, now you get government minder for every decision.

All of the "buying to shutdown competitors"- not possible - you don't have enough cash! Well I mean, it would be possible, but it would also carry huge risk. (As you don't have infinite cash reserves)

Keep your companies small and agile, stay focused on your primary initiative, distribute profits to your employees, build infrastructure, contribute back --- I like this.
children.textZhHtml:
嗯..这是一个有趣的想法。 我喜欢。

你有一家公司，它的价值低于X美元？ 你做你想做的事。 高于 X 美元，现在你的每一个决定都会得到政府的监督。

所有“购买以关闭竞争对手” - 不可能 - 你没有足够的现金！ 我的意思是，这是可能的，但也会带来巨大的风险。 （因为你没有无限的现金储备）

保持你的公司小而敏捷，专注于你的主要计划，向你的员工分配利润，建设基础设施，回馈——我喜欢这一点。

children.author: Frieren
children.textRawHtml:
> Legislators squashing monopolies and making rules to keep competition intact

You need both. Even restaurants are heavily regulated to avoid making people sick. To let restaurants make people sick until they go out of business seems a quick way to decimate your own population.

And yes, that everything is consolidated in a few monopolies makes everything bad and expensive. So, that seems a great thing to solve too.
children.textZhHtml:
> 立法者打破垄断并制定规则以保持竞争完整

两者都需要。甚至餐馆也受到严格监管，以避免让人生病。让餐馆让人们生病直到倒闭，这似乎是一种快速减少本国人口的方法。

是的，一切都集中在少数垄断企业中，这使得一切都变得糟糕和昂贵。所以，这似乎也是一件值得解决的好事情。

我只在 HN 上扮演外行，但似乎与保护 YouTube 等的安全港 DMCA 完全不同，因为谷歌拥有完全控制权？

children.author: dannyw
children.textRawHtml:
There's no inherent fraud or trademark infringement in advertising/bidding for search terms of your competitors. A classic example is Dominos bidding for 'Pizza Hut', and vice versa.

There may be trademark infringement when you use another company's trademarks. There are some exceptions, for example copy like 'Compatible with $X' or 'Learn why users are switching from $X to <you>' are generally fine. The line has been drawn over decades of court battles and case law.

At work, we've dealt with a few examples that go as far as falsely impersonating our brand.

Recently, we've started getting 'explanations' from these (usually fly-by-night operators) that it was 'unintended' and the result of AI targeting and optimization. Yeah, right.
children.textZhHtml:
针对竞争对手的搜索词进行广告/竞价并不存在固有的欺诈或商标侵权行为。一个典型的例子是多米诺骨牌竞标“必胜客”，反之亦然。

当您使用其他公司的商标时，可能会构成商标侵权。有一些例外，例如“与 $X 兼容”或“了解用户从 $X 切换到 的原因”之类的文案通常都可以。这条界限是经过数十年的法庭斗争和判例法得出的。

在工作中，我们处理过一些甚至冒充我们品牌的例子。

最近，我们开始从这些人（通常是不可靠的运营商）那里得到“解释”，认为这是“无意的”，是人工智能定位和优化的结果。是的，没错。
